items.title: Welcome to Mossy Memory Vault
items.content:
Welcome to Mossy's Memory Vault! This is your personal knowledge management system for Fallout 4 modding.

## What is the Memory Vault?

The Memory Vault stores tutorials, guides, code snippets, and modding knowledge that Mossy can reference when helping you. Think of it as Mossy's long-term memory.

## How to Use It

1. **Upload Knowledge**: Drag and drop files (PDFs, videos, text, code) to teach Mossy new concepts
2. **Search**: Use the search bar to find specific information
3. **Filter by Trust**: Filter by Personal, Community, or Official knowledge sources
4. **Export/Import**: Share knowledge packs with other modders

## What Can You Upload?

- **PDFs**: Documentation, tutorials, reference guides
- **Videos**: Tutorial videos (auto-transcribed)
- **Audio**: Spoken tutorials or notes
- **Text Files**: Markdown, code, scripts, notes
- **Code**: Papyrus scripts, JSON configs, XML files

## Browse Community Knowledge

Click the 'Browse Library' button to discover knowledge packs shared by the community. When new packs are available, you'll see a notification badge.

## Tips for Best Results

- Add detailed titles and tags for better searchability
- Include credit information for community knowledge
- Use trust levels to organize your sources
- Export your best guides to share with others

Happy modding! 🎮

items.title: Advanced Fallout 4 NIF Export Pipeline
items.content:
This lesson teaches a modern Fallout 4 asset pipeline built around Blender, Substance Painter, Material Editor, and NifSkope.

Step 1: Build a high-poly source, then bake detail onto a clean low-poly mesh. Keep smooth shading, clean UVs, and controlled hard edges before baking.

Step 2: Export Fallout 4-ready texture outputs using a PBR metallic-roughness workflow. Required maps should include _d.dds for base color, _n.dds for normal data with gloss or smoothness packed into alpha, and _s.dds for specular or auxiliary packed surface response.

Step 3: Import a similar reference NIF with Blender NifTools, then align your custom mesh to the expected hierarchy, weights, and vertex color behavior.

Step 4: Build a BGSM in Material Editor with relative paths to the exported textures and verify the required shader flags such as Specular, Specular_Lighting, Receive_Shadows, Cast_Shadows, and Double Sided where needed.

Step 5: Open the exported NIF in NifSkope, locate the BSTriShape or NiTriShape and its BSLightingShaderProperty, connect the relative BGSM path, then sanitize the file with Spells -> Optimize -> Clean Nifty String Index Table before testing.

Common teaching checks: black assets usually point to bad relative paths, empty packed alpha channels, or shader mismatch; instant CTDs often point to corrupted string tables or invalid material hookups.

items.title: Event-Driven Papyrus Performance Principles
items.content:
This lesson teaches modern Papyrus architecture for low-latency, low-bloat Fallout 4 scripting.

Rule 1: Avoid RegisterForUpdate() and RegisterForSingleUpdate() as default polling patterns. Prefer event-driven hooks such as RegisterForAnimationEvent(), RegisterForCustomEvent(), and RegisterForRemoteEvent() so the script sleeps until the engine sends an exact trigger.

Rule 2: Use Papyrus states instead of large repeated if/else chains. Put baseline behavior in an Auto State, switch into focused processing with GoToState("Active"), run the one-shot logic, then return to the idle state.

Rule 3: Practice strict array and memory discipline. Repeated runtime resizing is expensive, so prefer pre-planned arrays and F4SE-assisted native structures when the design needs heavier data handling.

Rule 4: Use short-lived quest orchestration for transient logic. Scripts attached to persistent actors or world objects remain in save data longer, so teaching should prefer quest-driven processing that starts, does the work, and stops cleanly.

Common teaching checks: if scripts stop responding, verify they are not trapped in a custom state; if stack dumping appears, move heavy work out of loops and remove polling-based architecture.

items.title: FO4 JSON Lesson Dataset: Asset + Papyrus Modules
items.content:
This entry defines a structured JSON blueprint for advanced Fallout 4 teaching. Module 1 covers high-to-low geometry targets, UV requirements, custom _d/_n/_s channel packing, BGSM flags, and expected NIF node hierarchy. Module 2 covers event-driven Papyrus architecture, anti-polling design, state transitions, and memory management constraints.

Use this schema to drive lesson generation, tutoring prompts, and consistency checks across assets and scripting instruction.

items.title: FO4 Engine Stability & Optimization Manual
items.content:
This lesson codifies two core stability tracks for modern Fallout 4 mod releases.

Track 1: FormID and plugin boundaries. Teach full-plugin slot limits, ESL usage strategy, and strict ESL-safe record ranges (0x000-0xFFF) to avoid overflow and corruption risks.

Track 2: Precombine and previs discipline. Teach that editing statics can invalidate optimization for entire cells, causing severe frame drops, and that world-edit releases must regenerate and ship valid precombine (.ucb) and previs (.uvd) outputs from Creation Kit.

items.title: FO4 High-to-Low Poly Baking Workflow
items.content:
This lesson defines a production baking workflow for Fallout 4 assets using explicit _high/_low naming, cage-driven projection control, and MikkTSpace-compatible tangent baking.

Core setup: maintain sharp edges across UV seams, apply weighted normals before baking, and keep high/low meshes perfectly aligned with matching pivots and transforms.

Recommended bake profile: 2048 maps for item-scale assets, 4096 for large structures, 4x4 or 8x8 anti-aliasing, and at least 16px dilation padding.

Troubleshooting focus: wavy normals are usually ray-direction or normal-basis issues (fix with averaged normals or custom cage control); black seams and missing detail usually indicate insufficient ray distances or incomplete sharp-edge seam setup.

items.title: FO4 Creation Kit Ingestion, Form Setup, and BGSM Workflow
items.content:
This lesson teaches end-to-end Creation Kit asset registration for custom meshes and materials. It defines the canonical folder layout under Data\Meshes, Data\Textures, and Data\Materials, and details form setup patterns for Statics, Weapons, and Armor records.

It also introduces Material Swap records as a runtime-friendly way to remap source and target .bgsm files without duplicating meshes.

BGSM workflow requirements: create new BGSM files in Material Editor, use relative texture paths only, configure smoothness/specular defaults for Fallout 4 shading behavior, and enable required shader flags such as Specular_Lighting and Receive/Cast Shadows.

Assessment rubric for tutor scoring: geometry budget compliance, texel density consistency, UV packing efficiency, and strict relative path sanity across all materials and mesh references.

items.title: FO4 BA2 Packaging, LOD Generation, and MCM Integration
items.content:
This lesson covers advanced Fallout 4 distribution packaging and runtime configuration patterns.

BA2 packaging track: separate General and Textures archives correctly, preserve plugin-name-aligned BA2 prefixes, and maintain strict root folder structure so resources mount automatically.

LOD track: generate distance-tier object LOD with xLODGen, build texture atlas outputs, and deploy resulting Meshes\\LOD and Textures\\LOD resources into the release pipeline.

MCM track: define configuration schema under Data\\MCM\\Config\\<ModName>\\config.json, bind controls to Papyrus-backed properties, and process setting updates through stable event-driven script handlers.

Troubleshooting emphasis: wrong archive type, wrong BA2 naming, or bad folder root structure can cause missing assets or streaming instability.

items.title: FO4 OMOD Slot Architecture, FUZ Lip-Sync, and Havok Collision Workflows
items.content:
This lesson teaches three advanced production tracks for Fallout 4 mod delivery.

OMOD track: implement the CO + OMOD + MISC triad, enforce AP/MA keyword mapping, and apply model/stat properties safely so workbench attachments mount and filter correctly.

Voice track: prepare clean dialogue WAV sources, generate .lip timing metadata, convert to .xwm, then compile both into .fuz payloads for in-game voiced lines with facial sync.

Physics track: create simplified collision hulls, assign Havok material behavior, and wire bhk collision nodes in NIF structures so world objects maintain valid physical interaction.

Troubleshooting emphasis: missing workbench entries usually indicate keyword/category mismatch, invisible attachments indicate bad model binding targets, silent lips indicate failed lip generation pairing, and ground-clipping objects indicate missing or malformed collision data.

items.title: FO4 Companion AI Frameworks, Leveled List Injection, and Projectile Shader Workflows
items.content:
This lesson introduces three advanced gameplay systems for Fallout 4 mods.

Companion track: build follower package stacks with conditional transitions, script-compatible companion setup, and reliable follow/sandbox/combat behavior switching.

Injection track: avoid hard record conflicts by using startup-quest Papyrus injection patterns that add custom forms to leveled lists at runtime.

Projectile track: build modern glowing projectile visuals with effect shader properties, emissive tuning, UV animation controllers, and correctly configured projectile forms in Creation Kit.

Troubleshooting emphasis: non-responsive followers usually indicate bad package conditions or alias setup, missing loot additions usually indicate broken property binding on injection scripts, and non-glowing/non-animated projectiles usually indicate missing shader blocks or controller mappings.

items.title: FO4 FOMOD Installer Architecture, F4SE C++ Plugin Setup, and Git Team Workflow
items.content:
This lesson introduces three advanced delivery and engineering tracks for Fallout 4 mod teams.

FOMOD track: build mod-manager-friendly graphical installers with valid info.xml and ModuleConfig.xml files, selection-driven file mapping, and dependency checks for missing masters.

F4SE track: establish a C++ plugin environment with proper SDK/toolchain setup, safe query/load handshakes, and controlled initialization hooks after game load.

Version control track: implement a practical .gitignore policy and Git LFS tracking strategy so large binary assets are managed safely without bloating repository history.

Troubleshooting emphasis: installer launch failures usually stem from incorrect fomod folder placement/casing, XML crashes usually stem from invalid ModuleConfig syntax, plugin load failures usually stem from version/interface mismatches, and oversized repos usually indicate missing LFS tracking patterns.

items.title: FO4 Automated Papyrus Testing, Water BGEM Shader Workflow, and Havok Cloth Constraints
items.content:
This lesson introduces three advanced implementation tracks for Fallout 4 creators.

Papyrus testing track: build quest-driven automated test runners, isolate runtime dependencies with script mocks, and write structured pass/fail output into filtered user logs.

Water shader track: author flow-aware textures and configure BGEM material properties for reflection/refraction behavior, depth blending, and stable shoreline transitions.

Havok cloth track: build helper bone chains, paint controlled deformation gradients, and tune cloth damping/angle constraints for responsive but stable movement in-game.

Troubleshooting emphasis: missing test output usually points to Papyrus logging initialization issues, broken water visuals usually indicate invalid material flags or texture wiring, and unstable cloth motion usually indicates incorrect constraints or node hierarchy setup.

items.title: FO4 Extended Dialogue Interface, F4SE Memory Hooks, and Custom Behavior Graphs
items.content:
This lesson introduces three advanced engineering tracks for Fallout 4 mod creators.

EDI track: bypass the hardcoded four-choice dialogue cap using Extended Dialogue Interface, build and bind XML layout configurations for custom screen layouts, and control button state at runtime with conditional Papyrus logic.

F4SE hooks track: configure a Visual Studio 2022 C++ environment, link against the correct F4SE SDK version pair, apply RVA-based memory addressing for engine function targeting, and use IDA Pro or Ghidra for reverse engineering address discovery.

Behavior graph track: author Havok .hkx state machines using 3ds Max and Havok Content Tools, wire graph variable triggers to Papyrus events, and configure rigid body constraints for collision-safe movement.

Troubleshooting emphasis: missing EDI dialogue entries usually indicate XML layout misconfiguration or incomplete FOMOD installation, F4SE plugin load failures usually indicate SDK version mismatch, and stalled behavior transitions usually indicate Papyrus event name mismatches against .hkx variable identifiers.

items.title: FO4 Developer Skill Assessment Framework: C++, Papyrus, and Integration Entry Points
items.content:
This lesson provides a structured skill-routing framework for Fallout 4 mod developers across three proficiency dimensions.

C++ proficiency track: measures readiness for F4SE plugin development, memory hook creation, and RVA-based engine address targeting.

Papyrus skill track: measures ability to handle complex game-world logic, event handling, and UI data passing through quest-driven scripting.

Integration capacity track: measures ability to bind native C++ functions to Papyrus using the F4SE VirtualMachine interface.

Entry point for C++ experts with limited Papyrus: focus on F4SE plugin infrastructure, learn the Fallout 4 object hierarchy, then use VirtualMachine binding to expose native functions to Papyrus callers.

Entry point for Papyrus experts with limited C++: focus on EDI dialogue layout, xEdit record manipulation, and existing F4SE API consumption without writing native memory hooks.

Entry point for beginners in both: start with Creation Kit quests and scripts, consume community APIs before writing hooks, and edit existing .hkx behavior graph states rather than creating new nodes.

Troubleshooting emphasis: C++ experts struggling with Papyrus object access should study the F4SE RE type hierarchy; Papyrus experts with EDI failures should verify XML layout paths and installation order; beginners with silent quest scripts should confirm Papyrus logging flags and quest start conditions.

items.title: FO4 Getting Started Checklist, F4SE Hello World Template, and Architecture Overview
items.content:
This lesson provides a practical getting started checklist and two working code templates that demonstrate the F4SE-to-Papyrus integration architecture.

Setup checklist: install Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ Desktop workload, download the correct F4SE SDK and align it to the target game version, install the Creation Kit and extract Base.zip source scripts, and configure Autodesk 3ds Max with Havok Content Tools for .hkx behavior graph export.

F4SE C++ template: implements the minimum viable plugin with F4SEPlugin_Version metadata struct and F4SEPlugin_Load entrypoint. Uses _MESSAGE for log output and targets a specific RUNTIME_VERSION. DLL must be placed in Data/F4SE/Plugins/ for discovery.

Papyrus event script template: a minimal ObjectReference script demonstrating OnActivate event handling with a player identity check and Debug.MessageBox confirmation. Compiled .pex output goes to Data/Scripts/.

Architecture overview: F4SE C++ plugins hook engine memory via RVAs and expose custom native functions upward through VirtualMachine::RegisterFunction. Papyrus scripts receive engine events and call down into registered natives. Creation Kit and EDI define the data layer that fires the events Papyrus responds to.

Troubleshooting emphasis: missing F4SE load usually means wrong plugin folder path or RUNTIME_VERSION mismatch; silent Papyrus events usually mean missing compiled .pex or script not attached in CK; missing MessageBox output usually means unreachable conditional branch or logging flags disabled.

items.title: FO4 Visual Studio 2022 F4SE C++ DLL Project Setup: Properties, Paths, and Linker Configuration
items.content:
This lesson walks through the complete Visual Studio 2022 project configuration required to build a valid F4SE plugin DLL for Fallout 4.

Project creation: create a new C++ DLL project, set configuration to Release and platform to x64. F4SE only loads x64 DLLs.

General settings: set C++ Language Standard to ISO C++17 (/std:c++17), configure output directory to keep DLL builds organized, and match Target Name to your plugin identifier.

Include and library paths: set Include Directories to the F4SE SDK include/ folder, set Library Directories to the F4SE SDK lib/x64/Release/ folder.

Preprocessor definitions: add WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN and NOMINMAX to prevent Windows header macro conflicts.

Code generation: set Runtime Library to Multi-threaded (/MT) to statically link the CRT and avoid runtime dependency issues in the game process.

Linker input: add f4se_common.lib to Additional Dependencies to enable _MESSAGE, _ERROR, and _FATALERROR logging.

Post-build event: optionally add an xcopy command to automatically deploy the built DLL to Data/F4SE/Plugins/ after each successful build.

Verification: build with Ctrl+Shift+B, confirm .dll exists in output, launch game with F4SE, and check the plugin log in Documents/My Games/Fallout4/F4SE/.

Troubleshooting emphasis: LNK2019 usually means wrong library directory or missing lib in Additional Dependencies; C++17 errors usually mean language standard set incorrectly in wrong configuration; DLL not loaded usually means wrong folder, runtime version mismatch, or x86 output.

items.title: FO4 Advanced F4SE: Complex C++/Papyrus Argument Bridging, Engine Event Listeners, and RVA Live Memory Access
items.content:
This lesson covers three advanced F4SE plugin development phases.

Phase 1 — complex argument bridging: extend the native function bridge to accept TESForm* (game object pointer), BSFixedString (interned string), and VMArray<SInt32> (Papyrus integer array). Always null-check TESForm* before accessing formID. Use NativeFunction3 template matching the Papyrus argument count. The Papyrus script declares the function native with no body; the matching script name and function name must exactly match the RegisterFunction binding.

Phase 2 — C++ event listeners dispatching to Papyrus: implement BSTEventSink<MenuOpenCloseEvent> to intercept Pip-Boy and other menu state changes. Register the sink via g_ui->menuOpenCloseEventSource.AddEventSink(). Get the VirtualMachine instance from g_gameVM to dispatch custom Papyrus events back to listening scripts. Define CustomEvent and SendCustomEvent in a Quest script to broadcast payloads to external script listeners.

Phase 3 — RVA live memory read and write: use RelocPtr<T> with a compile-time RVA offset to resolve the runtime-relocated engine address. Always null-check GetPtr() before dereferencing. Write only to verified data variables, never to code segments. RVAs must be re-verified against new game binaries after every patch using IDA Pro, Ghidra, or pattern scanning.

Troubleshooting emphasis: null TESForm* crashes mean Papyrus passed None and the C++ side must guard; silent VM call drops mean script name or function name mismatch in RegisterFunction; event sink not firing means InitializeEventListeners called before interface pointers populated; access violation on RVA means offset is stale for the current game version.

items.title: FO4 IDA Pro RVA Pattern Scanner, EDI Papyrus Dialogue Controller, and Thread-Safe Telemetry Dispatcher
items.content:
This lesson covers three advanced engineering topics across F4SE reverse engineering and Papyrus integration.

Phase 1 — IDA Pro Python RVA discovery: use idc.find_binary() with wildcard byte patterns to locate engine functions in IDA Pro 7.x/8.x/9.x. Subtract idc.get_imagebase() from the match address to get the RVA for RelocPtr. Wildcard bytes must cover address-dependent immediates that change between patches. Re-run against each new binary to verify RVA stability.

Phase 2 — EDI dialogue controller: import the ExtendedDialogueInterface namespace in a Quest script, register a custom dialogue handler via EDI_API:GetAPI().RegisterCustomDialogueHandler(Self) in OnInit, and respond to OnCustomDialogueRequest with a String[] options array of any size passed to DisplayExtendedOptions. The dialogue node ID in aiDialogueNodeId maps to the block ID defined in the EDI XML layout file. This bypasses the vanilla 4-choice engine cap.

Phase 3 — thread-safe telemetry dispatcher: use std::atomic<bool> for a lock-free stop signal, std::lock_guard<std::mutex> for scoped memory read protection, and F4SETaskInterface::AddTask() to queue Papyrus VM calls back onto the main game thread. Never call Papyrus VM functions directly from a worker thread. Call StopTelemetrySystem() and join the thread before DLL unload to prevent crash on game exit.

Troubleshooting emphasis: IDA BADADDR means pattern changed in new patch; EDI options not displaying means handler not registered before dialogue fires; EDI node ID collision means another mod uses the same block ID; crash on exit means thread not joined before unload; Papyrus events not firing from AddTask means g_gameVM not yet valid.

items.title: FO4 Papyrus Telemetry Receiver, EDI XML Layout Configuration, and VirtualProtect Memory Writer
items.content:
This lesson covers the final integration layer: receiving C++ telemetry in Papyrus, configuring the EDI XML layout for extended menus, and writing live engine memory from an EDI button selection.

Phase 1 — Papyrus telemetry receiver: a persistent Quest script declares CustomEvent OnTelemetryUpdate and a ReceiveEngineData(Float) function called from the C++ AddTask lambda. It broadcasts the value via SendCustomEvent to all external listener scripts. The Quest must be Start Game Enabled and not Run Once to keep the event channel open across sessions. Cast akArgs[0] as Float to retrieve the value in listener handlers.

Phase 2 — EDI XML layout: place ExtendedDialogueInterface.xml in Interface\EDI\ inside the mod archive. MaxVisibleItems sets the button count before scroll appears. VerticalSpacing controls row gap in pixels. PositionX/PositionY are screen-space coordinates. FontName uses Fallout 4 font tokens ($FontDF_B for bold). Color values are hex ARGB with 0x prefix.

Phase 3 — VirtualProtect memory writer: RegisterFunction binds CommitMemoryWrite as NativeFunction1 accepting a float. WriteEngineMemoryValue calls VirtualProtect to temporarily set PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE around the target float address, writes the value, then immediately restores original protection via the saved oldProtect value. The EDI OnCustomDialogueSelection event maps aiSelectionIndex (zero-based) to CommitMemoryWrite calls with specific float values.

Troubleshooting emphasis: CustomEvent not firing means Quest not persistent or VM null in AddTask; EDI showing only 4 items means XML file path wrong; VirtualProtect failure means guard page or insufficient permissions; crash after write means RVA pointed to code not data; wrong EDI selection index means off-by-one in ElseIf chain.

items.title: FO4 Pointer Validation & Crash Prevention, Release Archive Deployment Structure, and Async Telemetry Logger
items.content:
This lesson covers three production-readiness topics for F4SE plugin development.

Phase 1 — pointer validation and crash prevention: use VirtualQuery to fill MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION and check page state before any memory write. Reject pages where State != MEM_COMMIT, where Protect includes PAGE_GUARD or PAGE_NOACCESS, or where Protect lacks a writable flag. Wrap raw pointer dereferences in Windows SEH __try/__except(EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER) to catch hardware faults that C++ try/catch misses. GetModuleHandle(NULL) returns the Fallout4.exe base address at runtime for manual RVA resolution.

Phase 2 — release archive deployment: mod manager archives root directly to Data/ so do not include a Data/ prefix. Place the compiled DLL and optional INI in F4SE/Plugins/. Place compiled .pex scripts in Scripts/. Place .psc source files in Source/Scripts/ for community transparency. Place EDI XML in Interface/EDI/. All paths are case-sensitive on some virtual filesystems.

Phase 3 — async buffered telemetry logger: AsyncTelemetryLogger batches log entries in a std::vector<std::string> behind a std::mutex and flushes to disk only when the batch reaches flushThreshold. std::ios::app keeps entries across sessions. logFile.flush() commits the OS write buffer after each batch. The destructor acquires the lock and calls FlushBuffer() to drain remaining entries before file close. Initialize with a path in Documents/My Games/Fallout4/F4SE/ to co-locate with other plugin logs.

Troubleshooting emphasis: IsPointerSafeToModify false for known-good address means page protection changed in new patch; SEH fires means RVA is stale; DLL not found means archive has extra Data/ prefix; pex scripts missing means Scripts/ path depth wrong in archive; missing log entries after crash means flushThreshold too high for debug; interleaved log entries means FlushBuffer called without mutex.

items.title: FO4 Havok Behavior Graph Injection, Live WebSocket Telemetry Stream, and FOMOD Installer Configuration
items.content:
This lesson covers three integration and distribution topics for advanced Fallout 4 mod development.

Phase 1 — Havok behavior graph injection via Papyrus: Self.PlayAnimation(asEventName) sends a named event to the Havok state machine on the ObjectReference. The string must exactly match a transition event node identifier in the .hkx graph. OnMemoryWriteSuccess is a CustomEvent dispatched from the C++ AddTask lambda after SafelyWriteFloat returns true. The object reference must have a bound behavior graph assigned in Creation Kit. Define separate event node names for each mechanical state transition (Stage_Open, Stage_Close, etc.).

Phase 2 — live local WebSocket telemetry stream: BroadcastTelemetryData spawns a detached std::thread per call that initialises Winsock 2.2, opens a TCP socket to 127.0.0.1:8080, sends a JSON newline-delimited payload, then closes. WSAStartup must be matched with WSACleanup on all exit paths. Link ws2_32.lib via #pragma comment or VS2022 linker Additional Dependencies. For high-frequency calls consider a persistent socket on the worker thread instead of reconnecting every call.

Phase 3 — FOMOD ModuleConfig.xml: place fomod/ModuleConfig.xml at the archive root (not inside Data/). type=SelectExactlyOne forces a single selection; SelectAtLeastOne or SelectAny allow multiple choices. source is relative to archive root, destination is relative to Data/. priority controls conflict resolution between options. A companion info.xml provides mod metadata for the installer header. Add moduleDependencies to check for required mods before installation.

Troubleshooting emphasis: PlayAnimation no effect means no bound hkx graph or event name mismatch; OnMemoryWriteSuccess never fires means C++ side not dispatching after confirmed write; TCP connect fails means no listener running on target port; ws2_32 LNK2019 means library not linked; FOMOD not triggered means fomod/ folder not at archive root; files installed wrong means source path mismatch or extra Data/ prefix in destination.

items.title: FO4 HTML/JS Telemetry Dashboard, VS2022 Developer Debug Configuration, and Havok Graph Variable States
items.content:
This lesson covers three developer experience and animation integration topics.

Phase 1 — HTML/JS WebSocket telemetry dashboard: standalone index.html connects via new WebSocket('ws://127.0.0.1:8080') to a Node.js relay that bridges the C++ raw TCP stream. socket.onmessage parses JSON telemetry frames and updates the display with toFixed(4). socket.onclose shows a disconnected state. Open directly in a browser via file:// — no web server needed on the client side.

Phase 2 — VS2022 Developer Debug configuration: open Configuration Manager, create a new configuration named Developer Debug by copying settings from Release. Add _DEVELOPER_DEBUG to Preprocessor Definitions only for this configuration. Use #ifdef _DEVELOPER_DEBUG in C++ to gate heavy features (BroadcastTelemetryData) out of the Release binary at compile time. Set a separate Output Directory for Developer Debug to prevent overwriting the Release DLL. Never add the macro to Release.

Phase 3 — Havok behavior graph variable states: SetAnimationVariableFloat writes to named float variable slots in the .hkx graph to drive blend speeds and rotation targets. SetAnimationVariableInt writes to integer slots to drive conditional branch selectors and direction flags. Variable names are case-sensitive and must match the slot names declared in Autodesk 3ds Max / Havok Content Tools. Always set variables before calling PlayAnimation so transition nodes read correct values at the moment the event fires. Variables persist until overwritten.

Troubleshooting emphasis: WebSocket onopen never fires means relay not running; dashboard shows 0.00 means relay connected but not forwarding data; BroadcastTelemetryData in Release means macro added to wrong config; DLL outputs overwrite means Developer Debug output directory not separated; SetAnimationVariableFloat no effect means variable name mismatch or no graph bound; wrong speed on activation means variables set after PlayAnimation call.

items.title: FO4 Node.js TCP-to-WebSocket Relay Bridge, Live Actor Health and Coordinates Capture, and VS2022 Post-Build Archive Deployment
items.content:
This lesson covers three integration and deployment topics for the complete F4SE telemetry pipeline.

Phase 1 — Node.js relay bridge: server.js runs two servers: a raw TCP server on port 8080 for the C++ plugin (net.createServer) and a WebSocket server on port 8081 for the browser dashboard (WebSocketServer). socket.on('data') trims the buffer, logs it, and forwards to the active WebSocket client if readyState === 1. Install the ws package with npm install ws. Start order: node server.js first, then browser, then game. Update dashboard HTML to ws://127.0.0.1:8081.

Phase 2 — actor telemetry capture: CaptureActorTelemetry() dereferences (*g_player) and null-checks before accessing pos.x/y/z and actorValueOwner. GetValue(*g_healthAV) returns current health, GetBaseValue returns base. Call only from AddTask lambda after world loads, never from F4SEPlugin_Load. Serialises to JSON with newline terminator stripped by relay trim().

Phase 3 — VS2022 post-build deployment: post-build batch script uses mkdir with 2>nul to create BuildArchive folder structure silently. xcopy /Y copies DLL and EDI XML. Windows built-in tar with -a -c -f zips the archive; -C sets working directory so zip contains relative paths not absolute. Apply only to Release configuration. Add Source folder to tar args for Developer Debug builds.

Troubleshooting emphasis: ws not found means npm install ws missing; dashboard connects but no data means WebSocket client opened after game launched; CaptureActorTelemetry returns empty braces means g_player null before world load; health reads 0.0 means actorValueOwner not yet initialised; tar cannot stat means mkdir missing for that folder; zip has absolute paths means -C flag missing or wrong directory.

items.title: FO4 F4SE Trampoline Memory Hooks, Grid Dashboard with Coordinate Canvas, and Papyrus Automated Test Suite
items.content:
This lesson covers three advanced topics: 5-byte trampoline hook injection, a live coordinate-tracking HTML dashboard, and a Papyrus unit test runner.

Phase 1 — F4SE trampoline hooks: query F4SETrampolineInterface from QueryInterface(kInterface_Trampoline) in F4SEPlugin_Load. AllocateFromCodePage reserves executable memory. Write5Branch overwrites 5 bytes at the target RVA with a relative JMP and returns a stub pointer to the original bytes for calling back. Store the original as a typed function pointer and always call it at the end of the hook to preserve engine execution. Never skip the original call. Re-verify RVAs after every game patch.

Phase 2 — grid dashboard with canvas: CSS grid-template-columns splits the layout into a metrics panel and a canvas panel. Canvas width/height attributes set internal resolution independently of CSS display size. Scale Fallout 4 world coordinates to canvas pixels by dividing by 200 and offsetting by half canvas dimensions to centre the origin. fillRect with rgba(0,255,0,0.1) creates a fade trail; clearRect gives a clean single-dot display. Y axis is inverted: subtract from canvas.height/2 to match screen space.

Phase 3 — Papyrus test suite: Debug.Trace writes to the Papyrus log file requiring bEnableLogging=1 and bEnableTrace=1 in Fallout4.ini [Papyrus] section. Debug.Notification shows on-screen summaries. Attach to a Start Game Enabled Quest so OnInit fires on every load. Call RunAutomatedValidationSuite from a registered hotkey. Extend with additional TestXxx() functions for each data layer.

Troubleshooting emphasis: AllocateFromCodePage null means pool exhausted by other plugins; crash on hook call means typedef signature mismatch or original not called; canvas dots off-screen means scale divisor too small; CSS height mismatch means attribute vs CSS size confusion; Debug.Trace missing means Papyrus logging not enabled in ini; OnInit not firing means Quest not Start Game Enabled.

items.title: Navigating Next-Gen and Anniversary Engine Updates
items.content:
This lesson defines the critical technical differences between the 2024 Next-Gen patch and the 2025 Anniversary Edition update for Fallout 4 mod creators.

Core distinction: The Next-Gen Patch (April 2024) was a forced, free engine overhaul that changed the game compilation format, memory addressing, native 4K console support, and BA2 archive headers. The Anniversary Edition (late 2025) is a content bundle and UI upgrade built on top of the Next-Gen engine. It adds the Creations menu, bundles official Creation Club DLCs, and includes an engine bug-fix pass.

BA2 Header Version rule: Pre-Next-Gen tools output BA2 Header Version 1. The Next-Gen and Anniversary runtimes require BA2 Header Version 2. Packing with an outdated tool causes the modern engine to silently ignore the archive or crash to desktop. Always configure Archive2.exe or Cathedral Assets Optimizer to target Version 2 headers unless deliberately targeting the legacy community.

Face-Gen stutter fix: The initial 2024 Next-Gen patch introduced a severe engine bug where any mod altering an NPC facial data record via a plugin caused violent multi-frame stutter every time that NPC loaded into the current cell. The 2025 Anniversary engine update completely removed this bug. Instruct companion and custom character modders that face-data stripping workarounds are no longer needed provided end-users run the Anniversary-era engine.

Creation ID master constraints: The Anniversary Edition natively injects dozens of new .esl and .esp official master records into every player's game. Scripts must use defensive validation with Game.IsPluginInstalled() before referencing vanilla or bundled Creation properties to prevent FormID conflicts. Example: if Game.IsPluginInstalled("ccXXXFO4001-PipBoy(Black).esl") ... endIf.

F4SE address library compatibility: F4SE C++ plugins that target memory offsets mapped for the 2024 Next-Gen branch break on the 2025 Anniversary compilation update because offsets shift. Always update the plugin's Address Library target headers to match the current build version or use CommonAddressLibrary (CAL) database offsets. Never hard-code version-specific memory addresses without an address library abstraction.

Diagnostic checklist for invisible textures and CTDs on modern installs: verify Archive2 or CAO is configured for BA2 Version 2; confirm game version is 1.10.980 or newer; test with loose files to isolate the archive from the content; check xEdit for FormID conflicts with AE injected masters.
